;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–2021)|War in Afghanistan]]
**[[October 2020 Afghanistan attacks]]
***A [[suicide bomber]] targeting the convoy of Rahmatullah Yarmal, the governor of [[Laghman Province]], kills eight people and wounds 38 others. Yarmal survives the attack. [https://tolonews.com/afghanistan-166821 (TOLO News)]
*[[2020 Kyrgyzstani protests]]
**Violent protests occur in [[Kyrgyzstan]] in response to the results of yesterday's [[October 2020 Kyrgyz parliamentary election|parliamentary election]]. Kyrgyz police use [[tear gas]] and [[water cannon]]s to disperse protesters. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-54422884 (BBC News)]
**Anti-government protesters seize the presidential [[White House, Bishkek|White House]] and [[Supreme Council (Kyrgyzstan)|Supreme Council]] buildings in the capital [[Bishkek]]. [https://www.straitstimes.com/world/europe/protesters-seize-kyrgyzstans-seat-of-government-reports (''The Straits Times'')]
**Former [[President of Kyrgyzstan|President]] [[Almazbek Atambayev]] is freed from prison by demonstrators. [https://sputniknews.com/asia/202010051080676891-protesters-broke-into-area-of-parliament-and-presidential-administration-in-kyrgyzstan/ (Sputnik)]
*[[Second Nagorno-Karabakh War]]
**[[Timeline of the Second Nagorno-Karabakh War|Timeline of military engagements in the Second Nagorno-Karabakh War]]
***[[Azerbaijan]]'s [[Ministry of Defence (Azerbaijan)|Ministry of Defence]] says the [[Armed Forces of Armenia|Armenian Armed Forces]] are bombarding the Azerbaijani cities of [[Beylagan (city)|Beylagan]], [[Barda, Azerbaijan|Barda]], [[Tartar (city)|Tartar]], and [[Ganja, Azerbaijan|Ganja]]. Azeri [[artillery]] pounds [[Stepanakert]] for a fourth consecutive day, killing 5 civilians, according to an [[Al Jazeera Media Network|Al Jazeera]] journalist in the city. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/10/5/azerbaijan-armenia-accuse-each-other-of-hitting-strategic-cities (Al Jazeera)] [https://apa.az/en/frontline-news/Azerbaijan's-Beylagan-Barda-and-Tartar-came-under-fire-from-Armenia-332103 (APA)]

;Business and economy
*[[Animal welfare and rights in Israel]]
**The [[Government of Israel|government]] announces it will ban the animal [[fur trade]], becoming the first country to do so. [[Ministry of Environmental Protection (Israel)|Environmental Protection Minister]] [[Gila Gamliel]] says "Utilising the skin and fur of [[wildlife]] for the [[fashion industry]] is immoral". Anyone found selling or buying fur after the ban, with the exemption of [[ultra-Orthodox Jews]], will face a fine of up to [[euro|€]]18,500 or a year in prison. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-middle-east-54418334 (BBC News)]

;Disasters and accidents
*[[2020 Atlantic hurricane season]], [[Hurricane Gamma]]
**Six people are killed as Tropical Storm Gamma approaches the coast of Mexico. [https://www.accuweather.com/en/hurricane/tropical-storm-gamma-turns-deadly-as-it-inundates-mexicos-yucatan-peninsula/825143?scrlybrkr=7d9f12c8 (Accu Weather)]
*Two more people who went missing in France during floods are found dead on the coasts of [[Liguria]], Italy. Two workers in [[Bajardo]], Liguria, are dead after their vehicle crashes while cleaning floods-related debris. The total death toll for the violent storms rise to 13. [https://www.tgcom24.mediaset.it/cronaca/liguria/maltempo-liguria-escavatore-si-ribalta-mentre-rimuove-detriti-2-morti_23803420-202002a.shtml (TGCOM24)] [https://www.ansa.it/sito/notizie/topnews/2020/10/05/maltempo-settimo-cadavere-trovato-in-liguria_297d71a1-455e-45f8-a2a9-fb5e1e9c1a2f.html (Ansa)]

;Health and environment
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in North America]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Washington, D.C.]]
*****[[White House COVID-19 outbreak]]
******[[White House Press Secretary]] [[Kayleigh McEnany]] announces that she, along with two of her deputies [[Chad Gilmartin]] and [[Karoline Leavitt]], have [[COVID-19 testing|tested]] positive for [[COVID-19]] and will undergo quarantine. [https://www.cnbc.com/2020/10/05/trump-press-secretary-kayleigh-mcenany-tests-positive-for-coronavirus.html (CNBC)]
******[[President of the United States|US President]] [[Donald Trump]] returns to the [[White House]] to continue his treatment there after a three-night stay in [[Walter Reed National Military Medical Center]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/election-us-2020-54427390 (BBC News)]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in New York (state)]]
*****[[Governor of New York|New York governor]] [[Andrew Cuomo]] orders schools to close starting tomorrow in several "hot spots" around the state, including parts of the [[New York City]] [[Boroughs of New York City|boroughs]] of [[Brooklyn]] and [[Queens]]. This comes after COVID-19 test positivity rates rose above 3% in those areas for seven days in a row. Cuomo declined to close non-essential businesses and religious institutions. [https://www.cnn.com/2020/10/05/health/us-coronavirus-monday/index.html (CNN)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Mexico]]
****The [[Secretariat of Health (Mexico)|Health Ministry]] reported a record jump of 2,789 [[COVID-19 pandemic deaths|deaths]] and 28,115 cases in [[Mexico]], far surpassing the previous record of 1,092 deaths and 9,556 cases. The government said the record was due to a change of methodology which includes additional cases that were not reported from June. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-healthcare-coronavirus-mexico-tally-idUSKBN26R024 (Reuters)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Malaysia]]
****[[Prime Minister of Malaysia|Prime Minister]] [[Muhyiddin Yassin]] announces that he will undergo a two-week home quarantine, after [[Minister in the Prime Minister's Department]] [[Zulkifli Mohamad Al-Bakri]], who attended a National Security meeting he chaired on Saturday, tested positive for [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]]. [https://www.channelnewsasia.com/news/asia/malaysia-muhyiddin-quarantine-religious-minister-positive-covid-13203616 (CNA)]
****[[Malaysia]] reports 432 new cases in the last 24 hours, a new record of daily infections since the beginning of the outbreak. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-malaysia-cases/malaysia-reports-432-new-coronavirus-cases-biggest-daily-jump-idUSKBN26Q1AQ?feedType=mktg&feedName=healthNews&WT.mc_id=Partner-Google (Reuters)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Iran]]
****[[Iran]] reports a record 3,902 new cases, taking the nationwide total of cumulative cases to 475,674. At the same time, the country announces a record 235 new deaths in 24 hours, which takes the death toll to 27,192. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/health/iran-reports-record-daily-covid-19-infections/1996136 (Anadolu Agency)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in France]]
****The government places Paris and its [[Île-de-France]] region on maximum alert following a surge of infection rates, prompting Île-de-France to shut down all bars, gymnasiums, and swimming pools completely and all festive gatherings in establishments are banned from being open to the public effective tomorrow. The restrictions will last two weeks, but restaurants will remain open with strict health protocols. [https://www.bbc.com/news/amp/world-europe-54413563 (BBC News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Iceland]]
****[[Iceland]] orders all bars, gyms and entertainment venues to close, and cuts the number of people allowed to gather in public from 200 to 20 amid a rising number of COVID-19 cases in the country. [https://uk.reuters.com/article/uk-health-coronavirus-iceland/iceland-closes-bars-gyms-again-to-curb-coronavirus-spread-idUKKBN26Q1QE (Reuters)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Spain]]
****The regional government of [[Castilla y León]] announce to confine the cities of [[León, Spain|León]] and [[Palencia]] given the rising number of infections detected there over the last 14 days. The measure, which will take effect tomorrow, will include closing times for establishments at 11:00 p.m. local time with the last customer permitted to enter an hour earlier, and capacity in bars and restaurants limited to 50% indoors and 60% outdoor in a similar move that was implemented in [[Madrid]]. [https://english.elpais.com/society/2020-10-05/castilla-y-leon-confines-two-cities-in-the-region-due-to-rising-coronavirus-cases.html (''El Pais'' in English)]
*[[Nobel Prize]]
**The 2020 [[Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine|Nobel Prize in Medicine]] is awarded to [[Harvey J. Alter]], [[Michael Houghton (virologist)|Michael Houghton]], and [[Charles M. Rice]] for their discovery of the [[Hepatitis C]] [[Hepatitis C virus|virus]]. [https://edition.cnn.com/2020/10/05/health/nobel-prize-2020-winner-medicine-scn-intl/index.html (CNN)]

;International relations
*[[United Kingdom–Venezuela relations]], [[Venezuelan presidential crisis]]
**The [[Court of Appeal (England and Wales)|Court of Appeals for England and Wales]] overturns a ruling earlier this year by the [[High Court of Justice]] that stated [[Presidency of Nicolás Maduro|the government]] of [[President of Venezuela|Venezuelan President]] [[Nicolás Maduro]] did not have the right to access the [[Central Bank of Venezuela]]'s gold, worth more than US$1.8 billion, currently stored by the [[Bank of England]] due to the UK government's [[Responses to the Venezuelan presidential crisis#Recognition|recognition]] of oppositional leader [[Juan Guaidó]] as the actual president. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2020/oct/05/uk-court-overturns-ruling-on-18bn-of-venezuelan-gold (''The Guardian'')]

;Law and crime
*The [[People's Representative Council|Indonesian parliament]] passes a controversial [[Omnibus Law on Job Creation|job creation omnibus bill]] into law amid mounting criticism over its provisions on labour rights, indigenous community rights, and environmental protection. Labour unions and civil rights groups plan to hold [[Indonesia omnibus bill protests|large-scale protests]]. [https://en.antaranews.com/news/158253/omnibus-bill-passed-into-law-amid-mounting-criticism (Antara)]
*The [[Ethiopian Civil Aviation Authority]] bans all flights over the [[Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/10/5/ethiopia-bans-flights-over-new-dam-for-security-reasons (Al Jazeera)]
*Former [[Vice President of the Maldives]] [[Ahmed Adeeb]] is sentenced to 20 years prison and fined US$129,892 for corruption relating to the leasing of islands for hotel development. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/10/5/maldives-ex-vp-ahmed-adeeb-sentenced-to-20-years-for-corruption (Al Jazeera)]

;Politics and elections
*[[2019–20 Algerian protests]]
**Between 400 and 500 [[Algerians]] defy the ban on protests and march on the capital of [[Algiers]] to both commemorate the 32nd anniversary of the [[1988 October Riots|1988 pro-democracy protests and riots]] and renew calls for the [[resignation]] of the ruling [[military junta]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/10/5/hundreds-protest-in-algiers-despite-ban-on-gatherings (Al Jazeera)]

;Science and technology
*[[2020 in paleontology]]
**According to a study from ''[[Scientific Reports]]'', the [[Megalodon|Otodus megalodon]] was the largest [[shark]] to swim in Earth's oceans. Its body size was 15 meters (50 feet). [https://phys.org/news/2020-10-body-size-extinct-megalodon-shark.html (Phys.org)] [https://www.forbes.com/sites/davidbressan/2020/10/05/study-shows-o-megalodon-was-the-largest-shark-to-ever-swim-in-our-planets-oceans/#3129f82927da (''Forbes'')]
*[[Discoveries of exoplanets]]
**According to a research published in the [[Astrobiology (journal)|Astrobiology]] journal by [[Washington State University]] professor [[Dirk Schulze-Makuch]], there are 24 possible [[exoplanet]]s that are superhabitable outside the [[Solar System]]. [https://www.cnet.com/news/scientists-find-promising-superhabitable-planets-that-may-be-better-than-earth/ (CNET)] [https://scitechdaily.com/some-planets-may-be-better-for-life-than-earth-researchers-identify-24-superhabitable-exoplanets/ (SciTechDaily)]
*[[Tasmanian devil]]s are introduced to the [[Mainland Australia|Australian mainland]] for the first time in 3,000 years. [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/tasmanian-devils-released-on-australian-mainland/ (CBS News)]
